standard_prerequisites: The definition of capping with the first Chern class of an invertible sheaf, and the compatibility of that operation with proper pushforward
The scheme theoretic image of an integral closed subspace under a proper morphism, and the local finiteness of the images of a locally finite family
The case in which the morphism is a closed immersion on every integral closed subspace, and the equal dimension case where the Chern class of a pullback is compared with the pullback of the divisor
core_obligations: Observe that if the morphism restricts to a closed immersion on every integral closed subspace of the source, the statement is immediate from the definition of capping with a first Chern class

Write the cycle as a finite linear combination of distinct integral closed subspaces, take their images in the target, and form the coproducts of the subspaces and of their images, with the induced morphisms

Use properness and local finiteness to see that the coproduct morphisms are proper and that the images form a locally finite family, and use the initial observation to transfer the statement from the source to the coproduct and from the images back to the target

Reduce to the case of an integral source mapping dominantly onto an integral target with the cycle equal to the fundamental class, where the identification of the two sides is the equal dimension comparison of a Chern class with a divisor class
proof_roadmap: Record the trivial case where the morphism is a closed immersion on every integral subspace
Decompose the cycle and pass to the coproducts of the subspaces and of their images
Reduce to an integral source dominating an integral target and invoke the equal dimension comparison
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the projection formula for capping with the first Chern class of a pulled back invertible sheaf at source lines 2932-2943, label lemma-pushforward-cap-c1, whose proof occupies source lines 2945-2979. The proof first isolates a trivial case in which the morphism restricts to a closed immersion on every integral closed subspace, then reduces the general statement to that case by decomposing the cycle, taking the scheme theoretic images of its components, and passing to the coproducts of the components and of their images, using properness and local finiteness to keep every morphism proper and the families locally finite. This reduces to an integral source mapping dominantly onto an integral target, where the identification is supplied by the equal dimension comparison between a Chern class and a divisor class. The counted statement records neither the coproduct reduction nor the final comparison.
